summary:
FieldShift Maestro is an AI-assisted agricultural decision-support platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data."

The application helps farmers make informed crop-rotation decisions by combining NASA Earth observation data, historical climate records, soil characteristics, terrain, water availability, and agricultural crop requirements. Farmers can identify their fields using an address, PIN code, ZIP code, or by drawing field boundaries on an interactive satellite map.

Using NASA POWER, the platform retrieves a 35-year daily climate record for the selected region and evaluates three crop-rotation strategies: the farmer's current crop, a climate-resilient alternative, and a nitrogen-fixing legume. Each recommendation includes five performance scores, visible uncertainty ranges, confidence ratings, and a historical seasonal stress analysis across 35 years.

A modular, code-based multi-agent orchestration layer coordinates NASA data retrieval, crop suitability evaluation, scoring, and result synthesis. An AI advisor powered by Gemini and OpenRouter explains the computed recommendations in English or Hindi and supports what-if scenarios.

By translating complex Earth observation and agricultural data into transparent, understandable decisions, FieldShift Maestro aims to make climate-resilient agricultural planning more accessible to farmers.
details:
Project Overview

FieldShift Maestro is a location-aware agricultural intelligence platform that helps farmers evaluate crop-rotation strategies using NASA Earth observation data and supporting agricultural datasets.

A farmer can enter an address, PIN code, or ZIP code, select a location on an interactive satellite map, or draw the actual field boundary. The application retrieves relevant climate, satellite coverage, soil, terrain, water availability, and agricultural information for the selected location.

How the Solution Works

The application follows a modular, code-based multi-agent orchestration architecture.

1. Agent orchestration and data acquisition

A background orchestration layer coordinates specialized agents, executes the analysis pipeline, and streams progress updates to the user interface.

  • nasa_data_agent: Retrieves NASA POWER weather and historical climate records, and checks NASA CMR satellite observation coverage.
  • crop_agent: Evaluates crop suitability, planting windows, and crop-rotation alternatives.
  • evaluator_agent: Computes five decision metrics, weighted scores, confidence ratings, and uncertainty ranges.
  • synthesis_agent: Generates a structured, deterministic summary of the computed results.

These agents are implemented as application code, not autonomous LLM agents. They execute predefined tasks and deterministic calculations without making independent AI-driven decisions.

2. Historical climate analysis

NASA POWER provides recent weather information and a 35-year daily climate record for the selected geographical area. The application evaluates historical rainfall and temperature patterns, calculates seasonal stress, and identifies suitable planting windows.

3. Three crop-rotation strategies

The decision engine compares:

  • Baseline: The farmer's existing crop.
  • Climate-resilient: A suitable crop from a different plant family with strong performance across historically stressful seasons.
  • Nitrogen-fixing: A suitable legume that can contribute to soil health.

Each option is evaluated using five weighted dimensions: crop suitability, water availability, soil health, erosion risk, and economic potential.

4. Transparent uncertainty and confidence

Every recommendation includes a score, a visible uncertainty range, a confidence rating, and a 35-season historical stress chart. Data provenance is tracked to distinguish live, modeled, reference, heuristic, and unavailable inputs. Missing data is not silently fabricated.

5. AI-powered agricultural advisor

A Gemini-powered advisor, with OpenRouter free-model fallbacks, explains the computed results in English or Hindi. Farmers can ask hypothetical questions such as:

  • What if rainfall decreases by 30%?
  • What if the temperature increases by 2 degrees?
  • What if irrigation becomes available?

The application modifies the historical weather record according to the selected scenario, recalculates the crop scores, and asks the AI to explain the differences. Every numerical claim in the AI response is validated against the computed results. If validation fails, a deterministic template is used.

The LLM integration follows a provider fallback chain: Gemini primary, Gemini secondary, OpenRouter free models, and finally a deterministic template.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Makes NASA Earth observation and climate information more accessible to farmers.
  • Helps farmers compare crop-rotation alternatives using historical climate evidence.
  • Encourages climate-resilient agriculture and nitrogen-fixing crop rotations.
  • Makes uncertainty and data limitations visible rather than presenting recommendations as guaranteed outcomes.
  • Provides multilingual explanations to improve accessibility.
  • Supports scenario exploration so farmers can understand how changing weather and irrigation conditions affect crop choices.

Technology and Tools

  • Programming: Python 3.12
  • Application framework: Streamlit
  • Mapping and visualization: Folium, NASA GIBS, Esri World Imagery
  • Data processing: Pandas, NumPy
  • NASA resources: NASA POWER, Common Metadata Repository (CMR), Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS)
  • Agricultural and environmental data: SoilGrids, USDA SSURGO, SRTM, OpenStreetMap, JRC Global Surface Water, FAO EcoCrop and FAO-56
  • Climate data: Open-Meteo ERA5
  • Market and yield information: Agmarknet, Yahoo Finance futures, FAOSTAT
  • AI models: Google Gemini and OpenRouter free models
  • Orchestration: Python background threads, specialized code-based agents, event queues, and modular processing pipelines
  • Deployment: Streamlit Community Cloud
  • Development assistance: Claude Code

Project Links

  • Live Application: https://fieldshift-maestro.streamlit.app/
  • GitHub Repository: https://github.com/smritmix3/fieldshift-maestro
  • YouTube Demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kQd7gz7DV5A

Explore the live application, review the source code and architecture, or watch the demonstration to see FieldShift Maestro in action.

Creativity and Innovation

The central innovation is the integration of long-term NASA climate records with a transparent, multi-agent decision pipeline for crop-rotation planning.

Rather than simply displaying weather information or asking an LLM to recommend crops, FieldShift Maestro separates data acquisition, agronomic evaluation, scoring, and AI explanation into distinct components.

Its historical 35-season replay, visible uncertainty ranges, provenance-aware confidence scoring, and validated AI explanations make the recommendations more transparent and auditable.

The platform also accounts for differences in data resolution. Regional weather information is clearly distinguished from field-specific soil, terrain, water, and satellite context. This prevents regional estimates from being misrepresented as precise field measurements.

The result is an interactive decision-support tool that connects NASA Earth observation data to practical agricultural planning while communicating both its capabilities and limitations.
